verses.1:1: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, together with the bishops and deacons.
verses.1:2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: I thank my God in every remembrance of you,
verses.1:4: always in all my prayers for all of you, making petition with joy,
verses.1:5: because of your participation in the gospel of Christ from the first day until now,
verses.1:6: having confidence in this very thing, that He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Christ Jesus,
verses.1:7: just as it is right for me to think this concerning all of you, because I hold you in my heart, and because both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, all of you are sharers of my joy.
verses.1:8: For God is my witness how I yearn for all of you in the deep affection of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: And I pray this, that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and in all perception,
verses.1:10: so that you may approve what is superior, that you may be sincere and without offense for the day of Christ,
verses.1:11: filled with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ, for the glory and praise of God.
verses.1:12: Now I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me have rather led to the progress of the gospel,
verses.1:13: so that my chains became evident in Christ throughout the whole praetorium and among all the rest,
verses.1:14: and most of the brothers, confident in the Lord because of my chains, dared all the more abundantly to speak the word of God without fear.
verses.1:15: Some indeed preach Christ even because of envy and rivalry, and some also because of good will;
verses.1:16: some out of love, knowing that I have been placed for the defense of the gospel.
verses.1:17: But some out of rivalry proclaim Christ without sincerity, supposing that they stir up distress for my chains.
verses.1:18: What then? Provided that in every way, whether through pretext or through truth, Christ is proclaimed, in this too I rejoice, and indeed I will rejoice.
verses.1:19: For I know that this will result in salvation for me through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
verses.1:20: according to my expectation and hope that in nothing I will be put to shame, but in all confidence, as always, now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
verses.1:21: For to me, living is Christ, and dying is gain.
verses.1:22: But if I am to live in the flesh, this is the fruit of work for me, and what I should choose I do not know.
verses.1:23: But I am hard-pressed between the two, having the desire to be released and to be with Christ, which is far, far better;
verses.1:24: yet to remain in the flesh is necessary because of you.
verses.1:25: And confident of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy of faith,
verses.1:26: so that your rejoicing may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my coming again to you.
verses.1:27: Only live worthily of the gospel of Christ, so that whether when I come and see you or while absent, I may hear about you that you stand in one spirit, united in soul, laboring together for the faith of the gospel,
verses.1:28: and are in nothing terrified by adversaries, which to them is a cause of destruction, but to you of salvation, and this from God;
verses.1:29: because it has been granted to you for Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him,
verses.1:30: having the same struggle that you both saw in me and have now heard about me.
verses.2:1: If therefore there is any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any depths of compassion,
verses.2:2: make my joy full so that you share the same mind, having the same love, united in soul, thinking the very same thing,
verses.2:3: nothing through rivalry nor through empty glory, but in humility considering one another superior to yourselves,
verses.2:4: each one looking not to the things that are his own, but to those of others.
verses.2:5: For have this mindset in yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who, although He was in the form of God, did not consider it robbery for Himself to be equal to God,
verses.2:7: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in outward appearance as a man.
verses.2:8: He humbled Himself, becoming obedient all the way to death; indeed, death on a cross.
verses.2:9: For this reason God also exalted Him and granted to Him the name that is above every name,
verses.2:10: so that in the name of Jesus every knee may bend, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth,
verses.2:11: and every tongue may confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.
verses.2:12: Therefore, my dearest ones, just as you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but much more now in my absence, work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
verses.2:13: For it is God who works in you both to will and to accomplish for good will.
verses.2:14: Now do all things without grumblings and hesitations,
verses.2:15: so that you may be blameless and guileless children of God, without reproach in the midst of a depraved and perverse nation, among whom you shine like lights in the world,
verses.2:16: holding fast the word of life for my glory on the day of Christ, because I did not run in vain nor toil in vain.
verses.2:17: Yet even if I am offered in sacrifice upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice together with all of you.
verses.2:18: And in the very same way, you also rejoice, and rejoice together with me.
verses.2:19: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I also may be in good spirits, once I have learned the things concerning you.
verses.2:20: For I have no one so kindred in soul who will be concerned for you with sincere affection.
verses.2:21: For all seek the things that are their own, not those of Jesus Christ.
verses.2:22: But know his proven worth, that just as a son serves a father, he served with me in the gospel.
verses.2:23: Therefore I hope to send him to you as soon as I see the things concerning me.
verses.2:24: And I am confident in the Lord that I myself will also come to you soon.
verses.2:25: Yet I deemed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and coworker and fellow soldier, and your apostle and minister to my need,
verses.2:26: since indeed he was longing for all of you and was distressed because you had heard that he had fallen ill.
verses.2:27: For indeed he fell ill to the point of death, but God had mercy on him, and not on him alone, but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.2:28: Therefore I have sent him all the more promptly, so that upon seeing him you may rejoice again, and I may be without sorrow.
verses.2:29: Welcome him, therefore, with all joy in the Lord, and hold such men in honor,
verses.2:30: because for the work of Christ he drew near even to death, handing over his life so that he might fill up what was lacking on your part toward service to me.
verses.3:1: For the rest, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is indeed not tedious for me, but for you it is necessary.
verses.3:2: Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the mutilation.
verses.3:3: For we are the circumcision, who serve God in spirit, and boast in Christ Jesus, and have no trust in the flesh,
verses.3:4: although I myself have confidence even in the flesh. If anyone else seems to have confidence in the flesh, I even more:
verses.3:5: circumcised on the eighth day, from the lineage of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee;
verses.3:6: according to zeal, persecuting the church of God; according to the righteousness that is in the law, having lived without reproach.
verses.3:7: But the things that were gains for me, these I have considered losses on account of Christ.
verses.3:8: Yet indeed, I regard all things to be a loss on account of the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ my Lord, on account of whom I have incurred the loss of all things and consider them as dung, so that I may gain Christ,
verses.3:9: and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the law, but that which is from the faith of Christ Jesus, the righteousness that is from God in faith,
verses.3:10: so as to know Him, and the power of His resurrection, and the sharing of His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
verses.3:11: if somehow I may arrive at the resurrection that is from the dead;
verses.3:12: not that I have already received it or am already perfected; yet I pursue, if somehow I may take hold of that in which I have also been taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
verses.3:13: Brothers, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it. One thing, however: forgetting indeed the things that are behind, and stretching myself out toward the things that are ahead,
verses.3:14: I press onward toward the appointed goal, toward the prize of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:15: Therefore, as many of us as are perfect, let us think this way; and if in anything you are otherwise minded, God will reveal even this to you.
verses.3:16: Nevertheless, as far as we have reached, let us be of the same mind and remain in the same rule.
verses.3:17: Be imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who walk in this way, just as you have our pattern.
verses.3:18: For many walk, of whom I often told you (and now tell you even weeping) that they are enemies of the cross of Christ:
verses.3:19: whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their own shame, who have their mind on earthly things.
verses.3:20: Our way of life, however, is in the heavens, from where we also await the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.3:21: who will reshape the body of our lowliness, conformed to the body of His splendor, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself.
verses.4:1: Therefore, my brothers, most beloved and most longed for, my joy and my crown: in this way stand firm in the Lord, most beloved.
verses.4:2: I urge Euodia and I implore Syntyche to be of the very same mind in the Lord.
verses.4:3: Yes, I urge you also, genuine companion, help those women who labored with me in the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my helpers, whose names are in the book of life.
verses.4:4: Rejoice in the Lord always; once more I say, rejoice.
verses.4:5: Let your moderation be known to all people; the Lord is near.
verses.4:6: Be anxious about nothing, but in every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests become known before God.
verses.4:7: And may the peace of God, which exceeds all understanding, guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:8: For the rest, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are modest, whatever things are just, whatever things are holy, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good reputation, if there is any virtue, if there is any praise of discipline, reflect on these things.
verses.4:9: The things that you have both learned and received and heard and seen in me, do these things; and the God of peace will be with you.
verses.4:10: Now I rejoiced greatly in the Lord because at long last you have flourished again in being concerned for me, just as indeed you were concerned, but you were occupied.
verses.4:11: Not as though I speak on account of want, for I have learned, in whatever condition I am, to be content.
verses.4:12: I know how to be humbled, and I know how to abound (everywhere and in all things I have been instructed): both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to endure want.
verses.4:13: I am able to do all things in Him who strengthens me.
verses.4:14: Nevertheless, you have done well by sharing in my tribulation.
verses.4:15: Now you also know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in an account of giving and receiving, except you alone;
verses.4:16: for even to Thessalonica, once and twice, you sent for my use.
verses.4:17: Not that I seek the gift, but I look for the fruit abounding in your account.
verses.4:18: Now I have all things, and I abound; I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent: a fragrance of sweetness, an accepted sacrifice, pleasing to God.
verses.4:19: And may my God fill every desire of yours according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:20: Now to God and our Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:21: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:22: The brothers who are with me greet you. All the saints greet you, and especially those who are from Caesar's household.
verses.4:23: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

notes.1:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'in the gospel of Christ' (in Evangelio Christi), adding 'of Christ' where Greek manuscripts read simply 'in the gospel'.
notes.1:7: The Vulgate reads 'sharers of my joy' (socios gaudii mei), differing from the Greek reading 'partakers of grace with me'.
notes.1:8: Latin 'in visceribus' literally means 'in the inmost organs,' a biblical idiom for the deepest seat of affection and compassion.
notes.1:28: The Vulgate reads 'a cause of destruction' (causa perditionis), whereas the Greek reads 'a sign' or 'proof of destruction'.
notes.1:30: The Vulgate uses the perfect tense 'audistis' ('have heard'), whereas the Greek uses the present tense ('hear').
notes.2:1: The Vulgate joins 'depths of compassion' as a genitive phrase (viscera miserationis, literally 'inmost depths of compassion'), whereas the Greek has two coordinate nouns ('affection and sympathy').
notes.2:6: Latin 'rapinam' denotes 'robbery,' 'plunder,' or 'something forcibly seized'; the clause is understood in Latin tradition either as Christ not regarding equality with God as usurpation or not clinging to it as a prize.
notes.2:11: In a notable Vulgate-distinct reading, the Latin renders the confession as 'that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father' (quia Dominus Jesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris), rather than the Greek 'that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father'.
notes.2:17: The Vulgate uses 'immolor' ('am offered in sacrifice'), whereas the Greek verb refers specifically to being poured out as a drink offering.
notes.2:30: The Vulgate reads 'handing over his life' (tradens animam suam), whereas Greek manuscripts read 'risking' or 'disregarding his life'.
notes.3:1: The Vulgate reads necessarium ("necessary"), whereas the Greek text has asphales ("safe" or "a safeguard").
notes.3:3: The Vulgate reads spiritu servimus Deo ("serve God in spirit"), matching the Greek dative reading Theo ("to God") rather than the genitive Theou ("by the Spirit of God") followed in most modern critical Greek editions.
notes.3:16: The Vulgate preserves the longer traditional reading ut idem sapiamus, et in eadem permaneamus regula ("let us be of the same mind and remain in the same rule"), which modern critical Greek editions shorten.
notes.3:20: The Vulgate renders Greek politeuma ("citizenship" or "commonwealth") with conversatio ("way of life" or "conduct," echoing conversatus in 3:6) and includes nostrum ("our") before Jesum Christum.
notes.4:6: The Vulgate construes omni ("every") with oratione ("in every prayer and supplication"), rather than taking Greek en panti independently as "in everything."
notes.4:7: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive custodiat ("may ... guard"), framing the clause as a blessing rather than the Greek future indicative ("will guard").
notes.4:8: The Vulgate renders Greek semna ("honorable") as pudica ("modest") and hagna ("pure") as sancta ("holy"), and adds disciplinae ("of discipline") after laus ("praise").
notes.4:10: The Vulgate renders Greek ekaireisthe ("you lacked opportunity") as occupati eratis ("you were occupied").
notes.4:19: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive impleat ("may ... fill") rather than the Greek future indicative ("will fill") and reads desiderium ("desire") where the Greek has chreian ("need").
